findings.description: AI-04 requires the rejected candidate snapshot to be 'rejected with a sanitized error identifying the affected principal(s)', and the COORD audit requirement asks for 'principal/path identifier when safe'. build_identity_snapshot raises a bare SECRET_MALFORMED with no agent name, the refresh_failed event's principal_id is always the identity-reader itself, and test_audit_failure_matches_frozen_event_contract asserts the agent name is absent. With N keyed agents an operator cannot tell which document is empty, malformed, or a duplicate, and a per-agent AUTHORIZATION_DENIED (COORD-07) is equally anonymous. Agent names are registry data, not secrets. Carry the affected agent name(s) in the BaoCredentialError category or a separate sanitized log field (the event schema's principal_id can hold spiffe://.../agent/<name>) and flip the test assertion to require the name while still asserting the key value is absent.
findings.resolution: Attach the affected agent name(s) (never the key) to the raised error / warning log; adjust the contract test to assert presence of the principal identifier and absence of key material.

except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — failed candidate must not replace state
    code = (
        exc.code if isinstance(exc, BaoCredentialError)
        else ErrorCode.CONFIGURATION_INVALID
    )
findings.description: The blanket except maps every non-adapter exception (agents.yaml schema/validation error, DuplicateApiKeyError-style ValueError, FileNotFoundError, or a programming error in the loader) to CONFIGURATION_INVALID and logs only that code; the exception type and traceback are dropped entirely. Combined with the default reader factory raising CONFIGURATION_INVALID for a missing BAO_BOOTSTRAP_DIR, an operator staring at a 503 loop sees the identical 'CONFIGURATION_INVALID' line every 30 seconds with no way to distinguish 'bootstrap dir missing' from 'agents.yaml invalid' from 'bug'. Logging type(exc).__name__ for non-BaoCredentialError exceptions (or exc_info for that branch only) is sanitized and sufficient; adapter errors already carry only code/category.
findings.resolution: For non-BaoCredentialError exceptions log the exception class name (and optionally exc_info) alongside the sanitized event; keep BaoCredentialError logging code-only.

findings.existing_code: if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip() or key in result:
findings.description: A KV document whose api_key has leading/trailing whitespace (e.g. a trailing newline from a shell-seeded value) passes the check (only all-whitespace is rejected) and is stored unstripped. _extract_api_key strips every incoming header value, so that key can never match: the agent is silently locked out while /ready reports identity: ready and refresh_succeeded is audited. Either reject key != key.strip() as SECRET_MALFORMED (consistent with the 'exactly one nonempty string' contract) or normalise consistently on both sides.
findings.resolution: Treat key != key.strip() as SECRET_MALFORMED in build_identity_snapshot and add a unit case.

findings.description: ApiConfig.from_env now forces api_key_identities to {} whenever BAO_ADDR is set, but the Langfuse middleware still resolves trace attribution from that map, so in configured Bao mode every authenticated request is traced as 'cloud-agent'. Not an authorization issue (verify_api_key is the only auth path and it uses the snapshot), but it is a silent observability regression introduced by this package's config change. langfuse_middleware.py is outside wp-coordinator's write_allow, so this needs a follow-up or scope extension: resolve via the IdentityRuntime lookup (or the principal already attached by verify_api_key) when Bao is enabled.
findings.resolution: Follow-up: have _resolve_agent_id consult the installed identity snapshot in Bao mode; file as deferred work if out of scope for this package.

findings.description: BAO_ADDR is now a single switch that (a) selects the internal secret/coordinator loader, (b) requires BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID/SECRET_ID instead of BAO_ROLE_ID/SECRET_ID, and (c) makes the identity-reader snapshot the sole allowlist, which in turn requires BAO_BOOTSTRAP_DIR plus a delivered service-identity-reader bundle. A deployment that set BAO_ADDR only for the internal loader (the pre-change documented usage) will, on upgrade, fail profile load on the missing renamed variables and, once those are fixed, 401 every request and serve /ready 503 until the reader bundle exists, with CONFIGURATION_INVALID audited every 30s. This is consistent with D4/D5 (fail closed, no fallback) but the coupling is not called out anywhere an operator reads: docs/openbao-secret-management.md:186-187 still instruct exporting BAO_ROLE_ID/BAO_SECRET_ID for the coordinator, and skills/bao-vault/scripts/langfuse_env.sh still authenticates with the legacy names. Neither file is in this package's write_allow; the migration/docs package should own the note and rename.
findings.resolution: Ensure the deployment/docs package documents the three-way coupling on BAO_ADDR and updates the operator docs and langfuse_env.sh to the BAO_INTERNAL_* names (or explicitly records langfuse_env.sh as a deliberate legacy holdout).

findings.existing_code:
async def run_reload_loop(runtime: IdentityRuntime, interval: float = RELOAD_SECONDS) -> None:
    """Refresh off the event loop until the server cancels this task."""
    while True:
        await asyncio.sleep(interval)
        await asyncio.to_thread(runtime.reload)
findings.description: Every hvac call in the reader is bounded by BAO_TIMEOUT, but OpenBaoClient.ensure_session takes an unbounded blocking fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on <bootstrap_dir>/service-identity-reader.lock. If another process holds that lock (a second uvicorn worker mid-bootstrap that stalls, or a stuck sidecar sharing the directory), the reload thread blocks forever: no refresh_failed event is emitted, readiness silently ages past 120s into 503, and the loop never re-fires. The spec's 'any failed read emits one sanitized failure event' therefore has a hang-shaped gap. Acceptable for pca-02 given single-process deployment and the adapter being owned by another package; worth a bounded wait or a watchdog on reload duration later.
findings.resolution: Accept for now; consider a non-blocking flock with bounded retry in the adapter, or a reload-duration alarm in the coordinator, as follow-up.

findings.description: In the reviewed range (cdaef0ad..424cd958) grace expiry is enforced correctly and monotonically, but no openbao.identity.snapshot_expired event is emitted when the 120s window lapses; only the periodic refresh_failed events (with snapshot_age_seconds) reveal it. The event contract reserves that event for exactly this transition. Already resolved in the follow-up commit f1cd473b (fix(openbao): audit expiry and reject malformed internal data), which adds a lock-serialized one-shot expiry event; recorded here so the consensus step knows the reviewed range is one commit stale on this point. Note for that follow-up: it reuses error_code TOKEN_EXPIRED for a snapshot (not a token) expiry because the frozen enum has no snapshot-specific code; acceptable but worth a comment.
findings.resolution: No action on the reviewed range; verified fixed at f1cd473b.

findings.description: Positive verification, no defect: static-key bypass is closed on every path examined. verify_api_key and optional_api_key are the only HTTP auth entry points and both route through _principal_for_api_key; no other module consults config.api.api_keys for authorization (grep over src/); ApiConfig blanks the identity map and get_api_key_identities returns {} under BAO_ADDR; the runtime applies the 120s age gate before the map lookup (COORD-04); a None runtime under Bao mode denies rather than falls through; sanitized create_client/_load_secrets_openbao errors no longer echo hvac responses; and the internal AppRole inputs (BAO_INTERNAL_*) are read only by OpenBaoConfig, never by the identity reader, which uses PrincipalOpenBaoConfig and the bootstrap bundle (D5 separation holds).
